subject: Burmese python
title: A 20-Pound Bobcat Raided a 14-Foot Python's Nest and Got Away

scenes.text: A fourteen-foot python lost her whole nest. The thief weighed twenty pounds.
In Everglades National Park, raccoon sightings fell over ninety-nine percent as pythons spread.
In 2021, a trail camera was watching a python nest in Florida.
When the mother slipped away, a bobcat walked in and started eating her eggs.
She came back and coiled on top. The bobcat swiped at her and kept coming back.
Biologists counted forty-two ruined eggs. No animal in Florida had ever been caught eating python eggs.

description:
A USGS trail camera in Big Cypress National Preserve filmed a bobcat of about 20 pounds eating the eggs of a roughly 14-foot Burmese python in June 2021.
The bobcat returned over several days, even swiping at the python when she was back on the nest; biologists later found 42 destroyed eggs. It was the first record of any animal in Florida preying on python eggs, published in Ecology and Evolution.
Pythons are linked to a 99.3% drop in raccoon sightings in Everglades National Park.
Could bobcats help control Florida's pythons?
first_comment: Bobcat sightings in the park fell 87.5% after pythons spread, so this was a bit of payback. Who wins if they meet face to face?
